discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological band theory)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that time-reversal-invariant insulators with spin-orbit coupling have a hidden Z2 topological invariant. They predicted a quantum spin Hall phase with helical edge states protected by symmetry. Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental confirmation in 2007: quantized edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. These works showed that ordinary band insulators can be topologically distinct without magnetic fields. The idea quickly extended to three dimensions, leading to the discovery of Bi2Se3-family materials, and later to topological crystalline insulators, Weyl semimetals, higher-order phases and systematic topological materials databases. The field now looks at every crystal in terms of symmetry and topology. The discovery is conceptually deep, experimentally decisive, and has created an entire class of materials and a large worldwide research program, including proposals for topological quantum computation.
